Recommended Intervention: Replace the fixed bi-annual cleaning schedule with a conditional, data-driven cleaning trigger that targets only the lower row edges of the utility-scale PV plant. The system monitors daily yield degradation against a local irradiance baseline to identify when soiling losses exceed a pre-defined economic threshold. When triggered, the available water and labor resources are deployed exclusively to the high-risk lower edge zones during one of the two permitted visits. This intervention reduces annual soiling losses from the observed 12-18% range by focusing limited resources on the areas with the highest marginal yield recovery, rather than applying uniform cleaning to all panels.

PARAMETER: Trigger Threshold — 2.5% deviation from baseline specific yield — ASSUMPTION
PARAMETER: Target Zones — Lower row edges of array — ASSUMPTION
PARAMETER: Water Usage per Cleaning Event — 0.5 L per panel — EVIDENCE-BACKED [C2]
PARAMETER: Cleaning Frequency — Maximum 2 manual visits per year — ASSUMPTION 
PARAMETER: Monitoring Signal — Daily specific yield (kWh/kWp) — ASSUMPTION

The intervention operates within the rigid constraints of the desert-edge utility-scale site. By limiting cleaning actions to the two permitted annual visits and capping water usage at 0.5 L per panel per year, the proposal ensures logistical compliance. The shift from time-based to condition-based cleaning allows the operator to reserve water for the visit that occurs when soiling losses are most acute, typically following a dust event. This strategy directly addresses the concentration of losses on lower row edges, maximizing the impact of the constrained resources.

Falsification Test:
Protocol: Deploy the conditional trigger system on one 10 MW sub-array (n=10,000 panels) and maintain a fixed bi-annual schedule on a matched 10 MW control sub-array.
Test Temperature: Operating ambient range 15°C–45°C (desert edge seasonal variation)
Duration: 12 months
Sample Size n: 10,000 panels per sub-array
Numeric Pass/Fail Criteria: The trigger sub-array must achieve a 1.5% higher annual specific yield compared to the control sub-array while strictly maintaining total water usage at or below 0.5 L per panel and total manual visits at exactly two per year. If the yield difference is less than 1.0% or any resource limit is exceeded, the test fails.
